title: One org language authority: new teams inherit it, team overrides are explicit
acceptance: Org X has language 'de' (set through setOrgLanguage by an owner). createWorkspace('Late team', X) -> getWorkspaceDefaultLocale(lateTeam) === 'de' (today it is 'cs', the workspaces.default_locale column DEFAULT).

An owner calls setOrgLanguage('fr') -> organizations.default_locale for the caller's org is 'fr'; every team of that org resolves 'fr', including a team created AFTER the call; a team in a different org keeps its own value.

setWorkspaceDefaultLocale('en', teamB) writes an explicit team override -> teamB resolves 'en' while sibling teamA follows the org's 'de'; the org then changes to 'cs' via setOrganizationLocale -> teamA resolves 'cs', teamB stays 'en'; clearWorkspaceLocaleOverride(teamB) -> teamB resolves 'cs' again.

setOrgLanguage (the Organization tab's org-wide control) clears every team override inside the caller's org, so after setOrgLanguage('fr') no team of that org resolves anything but 'fr' - the same org-wide reach the fan-out loop gives today (org-actions.test.ts 'reaches EVERY team').

A workspace with org_id NULL (unlinked legacy row) resolves its legacy workspaces.default_locale; an unsupported value in the override, the org row or the legacy column degrades to WORKSPACE_LOCALE_FALLBACK ('cs'), never to an unknown locale.

Migration on a DB whose org-default teams hold legacy values 'workspace'='en' and 'ws-late'='cs' (created after the last language write): after ensureDb, organizations['org-default'].default_locale === 'en', ws-late carries an explicit 'cs' override, and getWorkspaceDefaultLocale returns exactly the pre-migration value for EVERY existing team. A second boot is a no-op: after setOrganizationLocale('de') and a re-open, the org row still reads 'de'.
Downgrade mirror: after setOrgLanguage('de'), workspaces.default_locale for every team of the org reads 'de', so an older image that still reads only the legacy column hears the same language.
premise: app/_lib/db/workspaces.ts:126-133 - createWorkspace INSERTs (id, name, org_id, type, created_at) and never writes default_locale, so every new team takes the column DEFAULT 'cs' from app/_lib/db/core.ts:1649, whatever language its org chose.
app/api/workspaces/route.ts:89 and app/_lib/signup-service.ts:73 are the two live createWorkspace callers - POST /api/workspaces (a new team in an existing org) and self-serve signup.

app/_lib/org-actions.ts:96-113 - setOrgLanguage is the ONLY language write and it fans the value out to every workspaces.default_locale row listWorkspacesByOrg returns at call time, outside a transaction (comment 94-95: 'a partial failure re-runs to the same end state'); an org-wide fact is stored N times and a team born later misses it.

app/_lib/db/organizations.ts:62-66 - setOrganizationLocale has zero callers (grep over app/, pipeline/, scripts/), and organizations.default_locale (app/_lib/db/core.ts:329) is never read: Organization.defaultLocale (organizations.ts:24) has no consumer. A dead second authority for the same fact.

app/_lib/db/workspaces.ts:50-57 - getWorkspaceDefaultLocale reads only workspaces.default_locale; it is the language of every no-cookie path: comms-locale.ts:43 (candidate mail for a NULL-locale entry), automation-run.ts:395, group-eval-run.ts:338, interview-kit-run.ts:129, agent-hire/transform-run.ts:83, api/agents/hire-from-need/route.ts:101.

app/_lib/comms-locale.ts:29-33 documents that a second workspace 'sets its own default_locale (Settings -> Organization writes it via setWorkspaceDefaultLocale)' - but no per-team control exists; setOrgLanguage writes all teams at once. The per-team shape exists only in tests: automation-run.test.ts:368-396, distribution.test.ts:148-149, comms-translator-tenant.test.ts:20-22 each give sibling teams different languages.

Because workspaces.default_locale is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'cs', a stored 'cs' cannot say whether the team chose Czech or simply never followed the org - the inherited-default-override signature failure (presence carries meaning the column cannot express).
rollback: Purely additive: one nullable column (workspaces.locale_override) plus a one-shot backfill of organizations.default_locale recorded in seed_marks. The legacy workspaces.default_locale column is kept and mirrored on every write (acceptance 7), so reverting the commit series returns to the fan-out reader with every team's legacy value correct; the orphaned override column and org value are ignored by the old code.
runner_up: Make workspaceId REQUIRED on this context's stores (channels, campaign, companion, workspace getters): the route-layer ratchet (app/api/route-tenancy-coverage.test.ts) cannot see lib-layer callers, and group-eval-run.ts:333 / automation-run.ts:389 record the same defaulted-tenant language bug fixed twice by hand.
body:
## Summary
The organization's language is one fact stored in N+1 places: a dead `organizations.default_locale` column nobody reads, and one `workspaces.default_locale` copy per team that `setOrgLanguage` fans out at call time. A team created after the last language write is born Czech (the column default) and every NULL-locale candidate filed into it is written to in Czech. Make the org row the authority, let a team follow it by ABSENCE, and make a per-team language an explicit, clearable override.

## Description
`createWorkspace` (workspaces.ts:126-133) never writes a language, so POST /api/workspaces and signup mint teams with `default_locale = 'cs'` (core.ts:1649) regardless of what the org chose. `setOrgLanguage` (org-actions.ts:96-113) papers over the split by looping every team row it can see at that moment - a snapshot, not a subscription - while `organizations.default_locale` (core.ts:329) and `setOrganizationLocale` (organizations.ts:62-66) sit unused. Six no-cookie paths (candidate comms fallback, automation passes, group eval, interview kit, agent hire) read the per-team copy, so the drift reaches candidates.

The move, per registry technique `settings/inherited-default-override`: (1) `organizations.default_locale` becomes the source; (2) a nullable `workspaces.locale_override` records a team's explicit choice, and absent means 'follow the org, continuously'; (3) `getWorkspaceDefaultLocale` becomes the one resolution door - override, else the org row via `workspaces.org_id`, else the legacy column for an unlinked row, else `WORKSPACE_LOCALE_FALLBACK`, validated at each step; (4) `setOrgLanguage` writes the org row once and clears overrides in that org (the Organization tab stays org-wide, as its test pins); (5) `setWorkspaceDefaultLocale` writes the override and `clearWorkspaceLocaleOverride` re-attaches; (6) the legacy column is mirrored on every write as the downgrade path (expand phase). A one-shot backfill seeds each org row from its oldest team and stamps an explicit override on any team that currently differs, so no existing team changes language at boot.

## Flow
1. Write the new test file with acceptance cases 1-7 against the current tree (expect 0 of 7).
2. core.ts: `ALTER TABLE workspaces ADD COLUMN locale_override TEXT` through migrateExec; the backfill runs once under a seed_marks mark.
3. workspaces.ts: resolver JOIN + override writer/clearer + legacy mirror; createWorkspace mirrors the org value into the legacy column.
4. organizations.ts: setOrganizationLocale writes the org row, mirrors legacy columns and clears overrides in one IMMEDIATE transaction (no await inside).
5. org-actions.ts: setOrgLanguage calls setOrganizationLocale(locale, orgId); the unlinked-legacy branch keeps the single-row write.
6. Fix the comms-locale.ts comment; update organization/README.md and localization.md (the two-authority list becomes 'org row, team override'). Keep org-actions.test.ts green unchanged except where it names the fan-out.

## Expected impact
A team added to a German org speaks German to its candidates from its first lead instead of Czech; the org's language is one row, not a loop that can half-apply; a per-team language becomes a real, clearable state instead of a test-only fiction. Closes the class 'org-wide setting copied per team at write time' for the one setting that reaches candidates.

## Evaluation
Claim: the organization row is the single language authority, teams inherit it by absence, and no existing team changes language on migration.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass.
After: 7 of 7.
Method: gate - node:test cases in app/_lib/db/workspace-locale-authority.test.ts plus the existing org-actions.test.ts, under npm run test:unit; tsc and lint on the combined tree.
Result: pending build.
Gate: architecture

title: Tenant tables key uniqueness by team: a derived gate, campaign_packs widened
acceptance: Gate: for every table in TENANCY_SCOPED_TABLES (eager tables after ensureDb, lazy tables after their store creates them), every PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE index either includes workspace_id or is listed in the gate's identity-key allowlist with a one-line reason; on today's tree the gate reports exactly campaign_packs (job_id,lang) and rediscovery_alerts (job_id,candidate_id) as offenders and fails.

Negative fixture: a synthetic table declared scoped with PRIMARY KEY (job_id, lang) and a workspace_id column is reported by the gate's pure checker with the table and key named; the same table with PRIMARY KEY (job_id, lang, workspace_id) passes.

saveCampaignPack('job-shared-corpus','en',packA,'llm','ws-a') then saveCampaignPack('job-shared-corpus','en',packB,'llm','ws-b') -> neither throws; getCampaignPack(...,'ws-a') returns packA and getCampaignPack(...,'ws-b') returns packB (today the second call throws 'could not be saved').
A same-team regenerate still overwrites in place: a second save for ('job-shared-corpus','en','ws-a') replaces packA, and ws-b's pack is untouched.

Migration: a DB created with the legacy campaign_packs (PRIMARY KEY (job_id, lang)) holding one row boots through ensureDb with the row intact under PRIMARY KEY (job_id, lang, workspace_id); a second boot does not rebuild again (guarded by the PK shape, like the channel_spend rebuild).

saveCampaignPack's upsert uses a target-less ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE campaign_packs.workspace_id = excluded.workspace_id, so the same statement succeeds against BOTH the legacy and the widened primary key (the downgrade and partial-rollout path).

rediscovery_alerts: team ws-a records an alert for (shared job J, candidate C) and dismisses it; team ws-b then calls recordRediscoveryAlerts(J, ..., [C], 'ws-b') -> returns 1 and ws-b's feed lists C (today INSERT OR IGNORE on the (job_id, candidate_id) index returns 0 and ws-a's dismissal suppresses C for ws-b).
premise: Adopts the open leftover 'Widen campaign_packs PK to include workspace_id' (.claude/scan-history/leftover-develop-2026-09-17.jsonl line 250, M, never built: no drain result names it, and campaign_packs' PK is still (job_id, lang) at app/_lib/db/core.ts:498-505) and generalizes it into the gate the defect class has never had.
app/_lib/db/core.ts:498-505 - campaign_packs PRIMARY KEY (job_id, lang); workspace_id was ALTERed in later (core.ts:1994) and is not part of it.

app/_lib/db/campaign.ts:33-41 - the upsert ON CONFLICT(job_id, lang) ... WHERE campaign_packs.workspace_id = excluded.workspace_id blocks the second team's own INSERT; campaign.ts:54-58 now throws rather than lie. app/_lib/db/campaign-tenancy.test.ts:47-56 pins that refusal, and its comment (lines 33-34) says it is reachable on '~100 seeded roles every tenant can open the Campaign tab on'.

The same defect was fixed by hand three times: app/_lib/db/core.ts:2465 (channel_spend), :2488 (analytics_targets) and :2521 (billing_usage) are one-off PK-widening rebuilds, each written after the collision shipped. Nothing derives the rule; tenancy.ts's TENANCY_SCOPED_TABLES asserts read/write filters, not keys.

app/_lib/rediscovery-alert-store.ts:44-45 - UNIQUE INDEX ux_rediscovery_alert ON rediscovery_alerts(job_id, candidate_id) omits workspace_id; recordRediscoveryAlerts (line 130) uses INSERT OR IGNORE, so a collision is a silent 0, and dismissal is sticky across the key (lines 251-252).

A PRAGMA scan of every TENANCY_SCOPED_TABLES table (ensureDb on a scratch KP_DB_PATH, lazy tables created from their store DDL) found natural keys without workspace_id on exactly campaign_packs and rediscovery_alerts; every other hit is an identity key (id, token, insertWithUniqueSlug slugs, hired_agents.report_token, Python-minted companion_brain_index.node_id) or a child key of an already-scoped parent (entry_id, session_id, posting_id, hired_agent_id) - the allowlist.

app/_lib/db/rollback-drill.test.ts:109-115 pins the three widened tables for downgrade compatibility; the rebuild helper app/_lib/db/core.ts:2419 (rebuildTable) is the established, transaction-wrapped shape.
rollback: Two independent halves. rediscovery_alerts: an index swap an older image never names (its INSERT OR IGNORE has no conflict target), so a code revert is clean. campaign_packs: the series lands the target-less upsert FIRST (works against both key shapes, verified on SQLite 3.53.4) and the rebuild SECOND, so reverting the rebuild commit leaves a working writer. A full revert to the old ON CONFLICT(job_id, lang) statement against an already-widened DB throws ('ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY'), so a complete back-out ships a reverse rebuild keeping one row per (job_id, lang) - packs are regenerable artifacts, not records - which is why risk is 7, not lower.
runner_up: Turn the companion proposal claim into a lease: claimProposal (companion.ts:515-523) sets status='accepted' with resolved_at NULL, and a process that dies inside spec.execute (api/companion/proposals/[id]/resolve/route.ts:129) leaves the proposal accepted-but-never-run forever, with no reclaim path and every retry a 409.
body:
## Summary
A workspace-scoped table whose PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE index omits `workspace_id` lets one team's row block another's on any shared id - and the shared corpus roles every tenant can open make that reachable. The repo has shipped and hand-fixed this defect three times (channel_spend, analytics_targets, billing_usage); campaign_packs is the fourth, still refusing a second team's save, and rediscovery_alerts is a fifth nobody noticed. Derive the rule as a gate over the tenancy manifest, and widen the two offenders it finds.

## Description
`campaign_packs` is keyed `(job_id, lang)` (core.ts:498-505). On a shared corpus job the second team to generate a pack gets a thrown 'could not be saved' (campaign.ts:54-58) - honest, but the feature does not work for them. The tenancy suite checks that every query filters `workspace_id`; nothing checks that a unique key does, which is why each instance was found only after it shipped. The move adopts the open leftover 'Widen campaign_packs PK to include workspace_id' and puts the rule where it stops recurring (registry `invariant-placement/placement-precedes-gate`: a rule re-broken at each new site belongs in a checker, not in reviewers' memory).

1. `tenant-keys.test.ts`: a pure checker (table, key columns, allowlist) plus a sweep over TENANCY_SCOPED_TABLES that reads PRAGMA table_info/index_list/index_info after ensureDb and after each lazy store creates its table. Allowlist entries are identity keys and child keys of scoped parents, each with its reason.
2. campaign_packs: the upsert becomes target-less (`ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE workspace guard`) - valid under both key shapes - then a `rebuildTable` step widens the PK to `(job_id, lang, workspace_id)`, guarded on the current PK shape so it runs once. The zero-change throw stays as the invariant check it now is.
3. rediscovery_alerts: drop `ux_rediscovery_alert`, create the same index with `workspace_id` leading; dismissal stays sticky WITHIN a team.

## Flow
1. Write the gate and the acceptance cases; run - the gate names the two offenders, cases 3/5/7 fail.
2. Commit A: target-less upsert in campaign.ts (cases 4 and 6 pass on the legacy key).
3. Commit B: the rebuild in core.ts beside the channel_spend/analytics_targets/billing_usage steps; add campaign_packs to rollback-drill.test.ts's widened set; flip campaign-tenancy.test.ts's second case to 'both teams keep their own pack'.
4. Commit C: rediscovery index swap in its store's own DDL block + the tenancy test case.
5. Docs: replace the 'GLOBAL constraint' paragraph in docs/features/jobs/README.md; name campaign_packs among the PK-widening rebuilds in docs/architecture/postgres-backend.md.

## Expected impact
Every team can generate and keep a campaign pack for a shared corpus role; a silver medalist dismissed by one team is still surfaced to another; and the sixth instance of the class fails CI on the commit that adds it, instead of being found by a second team in production.

## Evaluation
Claim: no workspace-scoped table can hold a unique key that lets one team's row block another's, and the two live offenders are widened.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass.
After: 7 of 7.
Method: gate - node:test in app/_lib/db/tenant-keys.test.ts, campaign-tenancy.test.ts, campaign-store.test.ts, rediscovery-store-tenancy.test.ts and rollback-drill.test.ts under npm run test:unit; tsc and lint on the combined tree.
Result: pending build.
Gate: architecture
